children: UBS analysts say they recently caught up with one of the largest U.S. cruise sellers, who noted clear skies, both figuratively and literally. The seller noted that August and September have marked a record in terms of inactivity during hurricane season, and as a result, booking volumes have been strong, the analysts say in a research note. The strength applies to fall cruises to the Caribbean, which is typically a softer season. It additionally applies to Caribbean cruises in the upcoming months, as well as summer bookings to Europe and Alaska for next year. Booking strength may stem in part from cheaper fares, the analysts say, adding that many cruise lines have been offering covert fares to stimulate demand. (connor.hart@wsj.com)
